args.summary: Following the v2.3.1 production deploy, checkout-api failed health checks in all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an 18% error rate. Rolled back all regions to v2.3.0, the most recent version that was healthy in production. Post-rollback verification: service healthy across all regions, error rate down to 0.2%. v2.3.1 should not be redeployed until the regression is identified and fixed.
args.title: checkout-api unhealthy after v2.3.1 deploy; rolled back to v2.3.0

trace.final:
Done. Here's what I did:

1. **Diagnosed the issue** — checkout-api v2.3.1 was unhealthy in all regions with an 18% error rate following the latest deploy.
2. **Identified the rollback target** — from the deployment history, v2.3.0 was the most recent version that was healthy in production (the intermediate v2.3.1-rc was only a staging release and was also unhealthy, so it was not a candidate).
3. **Rolled back** — v2.3.0 was rolled out to all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west). Since v2.3.0 was previously healthy in production, no change-manager approval was required.
4. **Verified recovery** — service is now healthy across all regions with an error rate of 0.2%.
5. **Opened SEV2 incident INC-0001** — documented the failure, the rollback action, and verification; the on-call engineer has been paged. Note in the incident that v2.3.1 should not be redeployed until the regression is root-caused.
